description: Sixteen sequencers in one module, each drawing a voltage sequence and a gate sequence of up to 32 steps, with all sixteen reaching the outside on polyphonic cables

params.text: Selects that sequencer for editing, so the display draws its voltage and gate steps

inputs.text: Advances the sequencers: a polyphonic cable steps each sequencer from its own channel, and a single channel steps all sixteen together
Sets the lengths, channel by channel, 0-10V for 1 to 32 steps; a sequencer with no channel of its own keeps the length it was given
A rising edge returns every sequencer to its first step, and clock pulses are ignored for the following 1ms

outputs.text: The voltage drawn at the current step of each sequencer, one channel per sequencer, in the range chosen for it
A 10ms 10V trigger on every step marked in the gate sequence, one channel per sequencer

notes: drag in the upper half of the display to draw voltages and in the lower half to set gates
Quick Key Reference in the right-click menu lists the keys the display responds to: f to freeze for editing, g to send a gate while frozen, and r to randomise the sequence under the pointer
every step of every sequence starts at zero, so the voltage output stays at the bottom of its range and no gate is put out until the display is drawn on
holding shift and dragging on the display shifts the sequence under the pointer left or right
menu: Sequencer Settings — All Sequencers, and Sequencer #1 through Sequencer #16, each holding that sequencer's Output Range, Snap and Sample & Hold
Snap — None, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 32 or 36, rounding drawn voltages to that many steps; reached through Sequencer Settings
Sample & Hold — Off or On, holding the voltage output between gates instead of changing it every step; reached through Sequencer Settings
Reset Mode — two choices printed Next clock input. and Instant, setting whether a reset takes effect on the next clock or at once
Output Range — the span of a sequencer's voltage output, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with; reached through Sequencer Settings
Quick Key Reference — lists the keys the display responds to while the pointer is over the module

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · stepped · polyphonic

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
